history.period: Antiquity uncertain; the monolith tradition spans centuries (verify)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. The Makhel Monoliths are a Naga megalithic heritage site at Makhel, a Mao Naga village in Senapati district (about 120 km from Imphal), NOT a Hindu temple. Makhel is regarded in Naga oral tradition as the ancestral home and first settlement of the Nagas — 'the birthplace of the Naga civilization' — from where the tribes dispersed. The Makhel Sacred Complex (Makhel Laikha) comprises stone monoliths (menhirs) believed to represent ancestors and deities of the tribe, used historically for ritual commemorations and to mark significant tribal events. Documented monuments include the 'departure stone of three brothers' (Pinoumau Ksii Tamara Tu): a 2.14 m menhir erected, per legend, by three brothers (Asupfualapha, Tuttowo, Khephio) before they dispersed from Makhel; it fell during World War II and was reinstated by the community (per a published archaeological survey). A platform stone beside the stone circle (Rashaba) served for the village chief's ritual announcements. In February 2018 the Manipur Tribal Affairs & Hills Minister inspected Makhel as a proposed 'heritage village'. The monoliths are Mao/Poumai Naga megalithic monuments of indigenous tradition — Meitei-origin narratives attach to the wider Koubru-Makhel sacred landscape, but the stones themselves are not Hindu shrines. Coordinates 25.2758 N, 94.090 E are from a published anthropological field study of Mao villages.

name: Makhel Monoliths
town: Makhel (CSV town 'Senapati' is the district; the site is at Makhel village)
town_description: Makhel is a Mao Naga village in the Mao-Maram sub-division of Senapati district, about 120 km from Imphal and close to the Nagaland border, at about 1,559 m altitude. Regarded in Naga oral tradition as the first settlement and dispersal point of the Nagas, it is a centre of Mao cultural heritage; the state government has proposed it as a heritage village.
tradition: Indigenous Naga (Mao/Poumai) tradition - NOT a Hindu temple

travel.railway: No railway station nearby; nearest major railhead is Dimapur (Nagaland) (verify).
travel.road: Makhel is in the Mao-Maram area off NH-2 (Imphal-Kohima highway); reached by road from Mao/Maram or Tadubi (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for clear weather in the Naga hills.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open site; no fixed hours - confirm with village authorities before visiting.
